column5: Progressive price indexing above the 50th percentile
column6: Progressive price indexing of PIA factors above the 50th-percentile AIME, for those newly eligible in 2033 and later

column6: For those newly eligible for OASI in 2036 and later, scale PIA factors by the ratio of life expectancy at 67 (longevity indexing of initial benefits)

column5: Base benefits on 40 years of earnings instead of 35
column6: Increase the number of computation years for retired workers and survivors from 35 to 40, phased in over 2027-2035

column5: Cut benefits 5% for new beneficiaries from 2027
column6: Reduce benefits by 5 percent for those newly eligible for benefits in 2027 and later

column5: Raise benefits 5% for all beneficiaries from 2027
column6: Increase benefits by 5 percent for all beneficiaries as of the beginning of 2027 and for those newly eligible thereafter

column5: Enhanced minimum benefit at 125% of poverty
column6: Reconfigure the special minimum benefit for those newly eligible in 2027 and later: PIA for 30 years of coverage set at 125 percent of the monthly poverty level, wage-indexed for later cohorts

column5: Raise benefits 5% at age 85
column6: Increase benefits by 5 percent for beneficiaries age 85 or older, starting in 2027

column5: Raise the retirement age to 68 by 1 month every 2 years
column6: Starting with those age 62 in 2027, raise the normal retirement age 1 month every 2 years until it reaches 68

column5: Raise the retirement age to 68 by 2 months a year
column6: Raise the normal retirement age 2 months per year for those age 62 in 2027 through 2032, reaching 68

column5: Index the retirement age to longevity
column6: Starting with those age 62 in 2027, index the normal retirement age to keep expected retirement years a constant share of potential work years (roughly 1 month every 2 years)

column5: Raise the retirement age to 69, then index it
column6: Raise the normal retirement age 2 months per year for those age 62 in 2027 through 2038 (reaching 69), then 1 month every 2 years

column5: Raise the payroll tax rate to 13.0% (2029-2034)
column6: Raise the payroll tax rate 0.1 percentage point per year from 2029 through 2034, reaching 13.0 percent

column5: Raise the payroll tax rate to 13.4% (2028-2037)
column6: Raise the payroll tax rate 0.1 percentage point per year from 2028 through 2037, reaching 13.4 percent

column5: Raise the payroll tax rate to 14.4% (2032-2051)
column6: Raise the payroll tax rate 0.1 percentage point per year from 2032 through 2051, reaching 14.4 percent

column5: Eliminate the taxable maximum (no benefit credit)
column6: Eliminate the taxable maximum in years 2027 and later, and apply full 12.4 percent payroll tax rate to all earnings (no benefit credit for earnings above the current-law taxable maximum)

column5: Eliminate the taxable maximum (with benefit credit)
column6: Eliminate the taxable maximum in 2027 and later, apply 12.4 percent to all earnings, and give benefit credit for earnings above the current-law taxable maximum

column5: Tax earnings above $250,000 (no benefit credit)
column6: Apply the 12.4 percent payroll tax rate to earnings above $250,000 starting in 2027 (all earnings once the taxable maximum exceeds $250,000), with no benefit credit for the additional earnings taxed

column5: Tax earnings above $400,000 (no benefit credit)
column6: Apply the 12.4 percent payroll tax rate to earnings above $400,000 starting in 2027 (all earnings once the taxable maximum exceeds $400,000), with no benefit credit for the additional earnings taxed

column5: Cover 90% of earnings (with benefit credit)
column6: Raise the taxable maximum so that 90 percent of earnings are taxable, phased in 2027-2036, with benefit credit for earnings up to the new maximum

column5: Cover 90% of earnings (no benefit credit)
column6: Raise the taxable maximum so that 90 percent of earnings are taxable, phased in 2027-2036, with no benefit credit for the additional earnings taxed

column5: Cover newly hired state and local workers
column6: Starting in 2027, cover newly hired State and local government employees

column5: Phase out the payroll tax exclusion for employer health premiums
column6: Starting in 2030, phase out the OASDI payroll tax exclusion for employer-sponsored group health insurance premiums, reaching full taxation in 2040

column5: Apply payroll tax to cafeteria-plan contributions
column6: Starting in 2027, subject contributions to voluntary salary reduction plans (cafeteria plans, flexible spending accounts) to the OASDI payroll tax, as 401(k) contributions are today

column5: Dedicate a 2009-level estate tax to the trust funds
column6: For deaths and gifts after 2026, restore the estate, gift and GST taxes to 2009 parameters ($3.5 million exemption, 45 percent top rate, unindexed) and credit all proceeds to the OASDI trust funds

column5: 12.4% tax on investment income above $200,000 / $250,000
column6: Starting in 2028, a separate 12.4 percent tax on ACA-defined investment income above unindexed $200,000 (single) / $250,000 (joint) thresholds, credited to the OASDI trust funds with no benefit credit

column5: Tax benefits like private pensions
column6: Starting in 2027, tax Social Security benefits like private pension income, phasing out the lower-income thresholds over 2027-2046

column5: Tax 100% of benefits above $250,000 / $500,000
column6: Starting in 2033, make up to 100 percent of benefits taxable (the remaining 15 percent) for filers with MAGI of $250,000 or more ($500,000 joint), thresholds wage-indexed, revenue to the OASDI trust funds

column5: Phase out income tax on benefits (2045-2054)
column6: Phase out income taxation of OASDI benefits credited to the trust funds over 2045-2053 and eliminate it from 2054 (HI revenue unchanged)

column5: Tax all benefits above $100,000 / $125,000
column6: Starting in 2029, tax all Social Security benefits for beneficiaries with income above $100,000 ($125,000 joint), thresholds CPI-indexed, revenue to the OASDI trust funds
